body.statement: Does \(q(v)>0\) for every \(v\in\Omega_V\), together with the calibrated restrictions \(\rho\ge\delta\) and \(d_M\ge\delta\), imply both that every moment vector of an arbitrary admissible SCM has an equal-moment representative in the bounded finite legal fiber and that every limiting vector of bounded graph-legal moments has an equal-moment finite SCM whose actual selected MAG remains in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\)? Resolve first the binary three-observed-variable COPAG with a compelled collider by stratifying the invariant essential-feature polynomials \(Z_e\). An affirmative resolution must give a legal lift for every boundary stratum; a negative resolution must give a positive rational \(q\), a rational \(\delta\), and an algebraic endpoint for which the negative certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) excludes every legal architecture.
body.justification: This is the sole nonroutine topological bottleneck between exact graph semantics and attained sharp bounds.
body.gap: Boeken, Forré, and Mooij show faithful laws form an open dense set, but their topology neither supplies an equal-moment lift on the unfaithful boundary nor produces an unattained causal endpoint.
body.consumer: Its answer determines whether exact-graph selection-COPAG bounds may be reported as attained sharp extrema without adding faithfulness or a minimum edge-strength condition.

obligation.what_is_open: For a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law \(q\), prove or refute that every arbitrary admissible moment vector and every limit of bounded exact-graph moment vectors has an equal-moment representative in the bounded fiber with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).
obligation.obstruction: The selected cell and intervention moments are linear in each source law separately, but a source-essentiality witness \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}\) is quadratic in the law of its own source. Ordinary \(m+3\)-point barycentric reduction can therefore send a positive essentiality polynomial to zero. Forcing finitely many witness values to retain positive mass is not justified at a boundary barycenter, and the frozen assumptions impose no faithfulness or minimum feature strength. Hidden-endogenous exogenization must additionally preserve actual functional dependencies rather than only a permitted latent projection.
obligation.attempted: The sourcewise reduction was augmented conceptually by all directed-feature indicators; those indicators are separately linear and can be preserved, but the two-copy source-feature polynomials remain nonlinear in the source being compressed. Retaining explicit witness pairs was also considered, but exact barycenter preservation with prescribed positive atoms does not follow on a proper face of the moment convex hull. The positive XOR support-deletion family confirms this failure of the naive route, although its illegal boundary has an equal-moment legal lift and hence is not a negative certificate. The compelled-collider test was solved only for an isolated selection root, as recorded in the partial result.
obligation.partial_result:
The mandatory collider test closes for the following nontrivial subcase.  Let \(V=\{X,Y,Z\}\) be binary, let the retained structural graph be \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\) with \(S\) an independent selection root, take \(B=\{X\}\), and assume the positive selected law \(q\) obeys the collider Markov restriction \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\).  Put
\[
 p_{xy}=q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y=y)\in(0,1).
\]
Choose independent \(U_X,U_Y\) with laws \(q_X,q_Y\), an independent \(U_Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and measurable sets \(E_{xy}\subset[0,1]\) with Lebesgue measure \(p_{xy}\).  The four sets can be chosen so that \(E_{0y}\ne E_{1y}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(y\), and \(E_{x0}\ne E_{x1}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(x\): begin with intervals of the prescribed lengths, and whenever an equality remains, exchange two sufficiently short subintervals between the set and its complement.  Positivity \(0<p_{xy}<1\) makes each such exchange possible, and finitely many disjoint exchanges preserve distinctions already installed.  Define
\[
 X=U_X,\qquad Y=U_Y,\qquad
 Z=\mathbf 1\{U_Z\in E_{XY}\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Pr(X=x,Y=y,Z=z)=q_X(x)q_Y(y)q(z\mid x,y)=q(x,y,z),
\]
and the two strict symmetric differences make both arrows into \(Z\) actual functional dependencies, even when \(q\) is unfaithful to one or both arrows.  Taking an independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), with \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\), gives \(c_v=\rho q(v)\) and \(d=\rho\).  For every bounded binary outcome map \(h\), truncated factorization gives the single attainable selected-intervention value
\[
 \theta=
 \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}q_Y(y)
 \bigl[h(0)(1-p_{by})+h(1)p_{by}\bigr].
\]
It is attained by the exact collider construction above.  Thus the exact-graph fiber and all its support-stratum closure points lift in this isolated-selection compelled-collider case.  This does not cover selected MAGs in which \(S\) has parents or latent ancestors, nor does it preserve an arbitrary pair \((n,d)\) beyond the value fixed by this collider factorization.
